title: civ4-advisor per-turn state
description: Specification for the JSON state file the mod writes each turn (one file per turn under a per-game folder in state/, e.g. state/LEADER_HATSHEPSUT_1738531200000/turn_0005.json) and for curated captures in samples/. The mod's Python 2.4 cannot validate against this; it exists as the contract reference and for harness-side validation later. All enum-like values are the game XML's Type keys (e.g. TERRAIN_GRASS, UNIT_SCOUT), so state joins directly against XML-derived rules data. Everything in this file is restricted to what the human player could legitimately see - never unrevealed map, other civs' internals, or anything else fog-of-war hides. COORDINATES: every x/y pair in this document uses screen/matrix convention, NOT the game engine's native one - (0,0) is the NORTHWEST corner, x increases east, y increases SOUTH. This is a deliberate inversion of the engine's own y-up coordinate space, applied once at export time (see game.mapHeight and the `map` section below); it exists because every prior attempt to teach the engine's native convention through documentation and printed compass bearings still produced agents narrating north and south backwards. Do not assume higher y is north.

schemaVersion.description: Bumped on breaking schema changes so the harness can reject stale samples. Bumped 1 -> 2 when every exported y coordinate was inverted (see the `map` section description): a v1 file read as v2 would render a silently mirrored map, so the harness refuses to load anything but schemaVersion 2.

trigger.description: Which event hook produced this export.

game.description: Game-level context, mostly static after game creation. The setup fields (mapScript, worldSize, climate, seaLevel, handicap, totalCivs, options, victories) are the settings chosen on the game-setup screen, which the player legitimately knows and which join against the XML rules data to give an expectation about a map that has not been explored yet. They are deliberately the setup PARAMETERS and never statistics of the map as generated - nothing here counts land tiles, resources or continents, all of which the engine would happily report and none of which a player can know without exploring.

gameTurn.description: The turn the player is about to play (see CLAUDE.md on export timing: exports fire at round end, labeled for the upcoming round).

year.description: Calendar year for gameTurn; negative = BC.

mapScript.description: Name of the map script that generated the map, e.g. 'Fractal' or 'Continents'. A script filename, NOT an XML Type key - along with map.tiles' plotType, one of only two enum-like values in this schema with nothing to join against.

worldSize.description: Joins CIV4WorldInfo.xml, which also carries the size-scaled tunables (city maintenance, tech cost modifiers, target civ count).

climate.description: Joins CIV4ClimateInfo.xml, which is what makes this strategically useful before exploring: CLIMATE_ROCKY carries iPeakPercent 35 and iHillRange 7 against 25/5 for temperate, CLIMATE_ARID adds 20 to iDesertPercentChange.

seaLevel.description: Joins CIV4SeaLevelInfo.xml (iSeaLevelChange: -8 for LOW, +6 for HIGH), i.e. how much of the map to expect to be water.

handicap.description: Difficulty, as chosen at setup (CyGame.getHandicapType). Joins CIV4HandicapInfo.xml for the AI bonuses and player cost modifiers it implies. Note per-player handicaps can differ in multiplayer; this is the game-level setting.

totalCivs.description: How many civs the game started with, i.e. how crowded the map is. CyGame.countCivPlayersEverAlive, deliberately not countCivPlayersAlive: 'ever alive' is constant for the game, so it cannot reveal that a civ has been destroyed before the player would know. Excludes barbarians and colonial vassals.

options.description: Game options switched ON, in XML order; often empty. Small field, outsized effect on early-game advice: GAMEOPTION_RAGING_BARBARIANS and GAMEOPTION_NO_BARBARIANS change turn 1-20 play more than almost anything else here, and GAMEOPTION_AGGRESSIVE_AI changes how risky thin defence is.

victories.description: Victory conditions enabled for this game, in XML order.

player.description: The human player's own empire-level state.

goldPerTurn.description: Net gold change per turn at current slider settings (CyPlayer.calculateGoldRate); negative = running a deficit.

beakersPerTurn.description: Research output per turn toward the current tech as the game computes it (CyPlayer.calculateResearchRate). Includes the hidden research modifiers - a bonus scaled by how many met civs already know the tech, +20% per known OR-prerequisite, and 1 free base beaker - so it is larger than the raw slider split of commerce. See REFERENCES.md 'Research-rate mechanics'.

current.description: Tech being researched; null when none selected (e.g. at game start before the first choice).

progress.description: Beakers banked toward current, as the in-game research bar fills it; null when current is null. Progress is stored per team (CyTeam.getResearchProgress), plus the player's leftover research from the previously completed tech scaled by the research modifier - the same term the game's own bar adds, and already credited by turnsLeft.

cost.description: Total beakers current costs this team (CyTeam.getResearchCost), i.e. the number shown in game after handicap/game-speed/world-size scaling - NOT the raw XML cost; null when current is null.

turnsLeft.description: Game-computed turns to finish current research; null when current is null. Approximately ceil((cost - progress) / beakersPerTurn) but not exactly: the engine recomputes overflow crediting internally.

bonuses.description: Resources connected to the player's trade network anywhere in the empire, grouped by what they do, plus per-resource quantities. A resource sitting unimproved or unroaded in the ground is NOT here - it is in map.tiles; this section is what the trade network actually delivers. QUANTITY IS A PLAYER-LEVEL FACT and deliberately appears only here, never on a city: the engine tracks how many of a resource the empire has, while a city merely has the connection or does not. The count is what matters for trading a spare away and is meaningless inside a city. See cities[].bonuses for the per-city membership, which uses the same three groups.

strategic.description: Resources some unit or building requires in order to be built - the ones that gate what you can produce. There is no bStrategic flag in the XML and no isStrategic() in the API (CvBonusInfo exposes no reverse index either), so this is derived by sweeping every unit and building for its prerequisite bonuses, in both forms: getPrereqAndBonus, a single required resource, and the getPrereqOrBonuses array of alternatives any one of which suffices (the Spearman's Bronze/Iron/Horse). Derived rather than hardcoded by name so it stays correct if resources are ever added or retuned.

happiness.description: Resources whose XML iHappiness is positive - the luxuries a city's happiness bar credits when they are connected. Strictly positive, not merely non-zero: the engine permits a negative iHappiness, and listing such a resource here would read as a benefit.

health.description: Resources whose XML iHealth is positive - the food/health resources a city's health bar credits when connected. Same strictly-positive rule as happiness.

counts.description: How many of each connected resource the empire has (CyPlayer.getNumAvailableBonuses), for resources with at least one. Sits beside the grouped lists rather than replacing them: the lists answer 'what do I have', the counts answer 'what can I spare'. Keys here are every connected resource including pure trade goods, so this is a superset of the three lists above.

units.description: The player's own units. FIELD OMISSION IS MEANINGFUL HERE, as in map.tiles: damage is written only when the unit is actually hurt, since undamaged is overwhelmingly the common case. Every other field is unconditional.

id.description: Engine unit ID, stable across turns for tracking.

moves.description: Total moves the unit gets per turn (CyUnit.baseMoves), including promotion and team domain bonuses - NOT moves remaining. Moves-remaining is deliberately not exported: the per-turn reset happens after our export hook fires, so CyUnit.movesLeft() would always describe the turn that just ended rather than the one this file is labelled for.

damage.description: Percentage of health lost, not hit points: 100 would be dead. Omitted when the unit is undamaged, which is its default and by far the usual case. PREDICTS the value AFTER this turn's heal, not the raw value CyUnit.getDamage() holds at export time: CvUnit::doTurn() heals a hurt unit in the same pass that resets moves, which runs after the export hook fires and before the player regains control, so the raw value always describes the turn that just ended. CyUnit exposes no healRate() to read the post-heal figure directly, so it is reconstructed from the exposed components of the engine's own formula (territory, promotions, and a nearby Medic-line bonus). ONE KNOWN GAP: a city's building-derived heal bonus (e.g. an Aqueduct) has no Python binding and cannot be reconstructed, so a unit garrisoned in such a city will in reality heal faster than this predicts - a bounded, permanent undercount for that one case. Foreign units' damage (foreignUnits[].damage below) is NOT predicted this way and stays live-read. See AdvisorStateWriter._setIfDamaged and _healRate.

level.description: CyUnit.getLevel(), incremented by exactly one each time a promotion is picked (verified in CvUnit::promote(), which calls changeLevel(1) alongside granting the promotion - never incremented automatically from banked XP alone). Starts at 1 for a fresh unit. Omitted at the default, the common case for a unit that has never promoted.

experience.description: XP banked (CyUnit.getExperience), toward the next promotion. Omitted when zero, which is the common case for a unit that hasn't fought.

experienceToNextLevel.description: How much more XP this unit needs before its FIRST promotion pick is funded. Mutually exclusive with promotionsAvailable by construction - present only while promotionsAvailable is absent, never reporting the distance to a later pick once one is already funded. See promotionsAvailable for how this is computed.

promotions.description: Promotions this unit has, as PROMOTION_ Type keys (CyUnit.isHasPromotion, swept over every promotion in CIV4PromotionInfos.xml, the same enum-sweep pattern as player.knownTechs). Export the inputs, not the verdict: combat odds against a given enemy stay the agent's judgement, but which promotions a unit has is not derivable from anything else in the file. Omitted when empty, which is the common case for an unpromoted unit.

promotionsAvailable.description: How many promotion picks this unit's banked XP currently funds - what the UI's XP bar shows as multiple markers past the current level (e.g. a level-1 unit sitting on 6 XP has funded 2 more picks, since level 1->2 costs 2 and level 2->3 costs 5). This is an UPPER BOUND on picks available, not a guarantee: it answers whether the XP exists, but not whether an eligible promotion actually exists at each hypothetical level - that depends on this unit's specific promotion tree, unit-combat class and prerequisites (CyUnit.canAcquirePromotionAny), which this field does not evaluate. A unit can show promotionsAvailable > 0 while genuinely having nothing left it is eligible for. Computed from experience by walking the same level-cost formula CyUnit.experienceNeeded() uses (iLevel*iLevel + 1, then the player's getLevelExperienceModifier applied), because experienceNeeded() itself only answers for the unit's OWN current level - there is no engine call to ask about a hypothetical one. Formula sourced from CvGameUtils.py's getExperienceNeeded and cited in REFERENCES.md; this is the schema's second documented exception (after map.tiles' plotType) to 'export what the engine computes, never re-derive it' - justified the same way, because there is no engine getter to read instead. Omitted when zero, the common case.

activity.description: The unit's standing order (CySelectionGroup.getActivityType), as an ActivityTypes key. A SEPARATE MECHANISM from `mission` below, not covered by it: fortify, sleep, heal and sentry each set an activity and then delete their mission from the queue (CvSelectionGroup.cpp:1014-1056, every branch 'bDelete = true'), so by export time such a unit has an empty mission queue. Without this field a dug-in unit and an idle one are indistinguishable. Omitted at the default ACTIVITY_AWAKE - a unit under orders or simply idle. NOTE FORTIFY AND SLEEP BOTH REPORT ACTIVITY_SLEEP (CvSelectionGroup.cpp:1018-1029) - the engine has no separate fortify activity, so this field ALONE CANNOT tell a fortified unit from a sleeping one; use fortifyTurns for that. Activities out of scope this early (NO_ACTIVITY, and the air/naval/plunder ones) are omitted rather than given an invented name.

fortifyTurns.description: Turns this unit has spent fortified (CyUnit.getFortifyTurns), 1-5. Omitted at 0, meaning not fortified - which is also how a SLEEPING unit is told apart from a fortified one, since both report activity ACTIVITY_SLEEP. This is a combat input, not just a flag: the engine's defence bonus is getFortifyTurns() * FORTIFY_MODIFIER_PER_TURN (CvUnit.cpp:8584), i.e. +5% per turn in this install's GlobalDefines.xml, capped by MAX_FORTIFY_TURNS at 5 turns / +25%. Exported as the raw turn count rather than the computed percentage, keeping the 'export the inputs, not the verdict' line - join it against the XML constants the same way as anything else. Read off the unit rather than its group, so it is still exported for a unit whose group is unavailable.

mission.description: What this unit has been ORDERED to do - the head of the engine's mission queue (CySelectionGroup.getMissionType/getMissionData1/getMissionData2 via CyUnit.getGroup). Omitted entirely when the unit has no orders queued, which is the common case for a unit awaiting instructions. This is the one activity fact no other field implies: a Worker halfway through a Farm and an idle Worker standing on the same tile are otherwise identical in this export, and a unit walking a multi-turn path looks the same as one standing still. HEAD ONLY, not the whole queue: the engine's queue can hold several shift-clicked missions and the game's own interface renders all but the first as '...' with no detail (CvMainInterface.py:2713-2737), so exporting the head matches both the display and the single-valued shape cities[].producing already uses. Which payload fields are present depends on the mission type, because the engine's iData1/iData2 pair means different things per mission - see each field below.

type.description: The mission's Type key from CIV4MissionInfos.xml (e.g. MISSION_BUILD, MISSION_MOVE_TO, MISSION_FORTIFY, MISSION_SENTRY, MISSION_HEAL, MISSION_SKIP). Always present. For most missions the type alone is the whole fact - fortify, sleep, heal and sentry carry no meaningful data payload.

build.description: What is being built, as a BUILD_ Type key from CIV4BuildInfos.xml (e.g. BUILD_FARM, BUILD_ROAD, BUILD_MINE). Present only for build missions - those whose CIV4MissionInfos.xml entry has isBuild() true, in practice MISSION_BUILD. Joins against the XML for the improvement produced and its yields.

turnsLeft.description: Turns of work still remaining on a build mission, PROSPECTIVE: turnsLeft == 1 means the build completes during the turn this file is labelled for, unless the player cancels the order or re-tasks the unit first - the player holds the whole turn to intervene. turnsLeft == 3 means it ticks to 2 during this turn on the same condition. Present only alongside `build`. CORRECTED BY -1 FROM THE ENGINE'S RAW FIGURE for a worker that has already worked this turn, which is not a staleness fix of the units[].moves / units[].damage kind but an artifact of the engine's own arithmetic meeting our export timing. CvPlot::getBuildTurnsLeft (CvPlot.cpp:2441-2492) ends with an unconditional iTurnsLeft++, because the game's interface reads it MID-TURN while the player is deciding and before this turn's work has landed; to stay consistent it first subtracts a 'now' build rate, but only from workers that can still move ('if (pLoopUnit->canMove())', and workRate(false) repeats the same gate at CvUnit.cpp:7409-7415). Mid-turn the two halves cancel. At our export timing (onEndGameTurn) a worker that spent its turn building can no longer move, so the subtraction never happens and the trailing ++ double-counts the turn in progress. Confirmed in live play in both directions: a 5-turn Farm one turn in reported a raw 5 (true answer 4) and a build about to complete reported a raw 2 (true answer 1). The correction is gated on the engine's own canMove() discriminator rather than applied unconditionally, because a worker ordered to build but not yet acted this turn had its 'now' rate subtracted normally and is already correct. It is also skipped when the raw figure is 1, since getBuildTurnsLeft returns std::max(1, ...) and a floored 1 cannot be told from a genuine one - subtracting there would claim a finished build. See AdvisorStateWriter._buildTurnsLeftOvercount.

destination.description: The plot this unit has been ordered to move to. Present only for MISSION_MOVE_TO and MISSION_ROUTE_TO, whose iData1/iData2 pair is a destination plot (verified in the BTS SDK source, CvSelectionGroup.cpp:1577-1582 and :1431, not inferred from the mission's name). A unit with a destination is mid-path across multiple turns; without this field a multi-turn move is indistinguishable from a unit standing still. NOTE there is deliberately no turns-to-arrive companion to turnsLeft: the engine repaths every turn and caches no ETA, so no getMoveTurnsLeft exists to read, and deriving one would mean reimplementing pathfinding - out of scope. `y` here is inverted to match this schema's north-up convention exactly like every other exported coordinate.

targetUnitId.description: The unit this one has been ordered to move to (e.g. a Warrior escorting a Settler), joining against units[].id. Present only for MISSION_MOVE_TO_UNIT, AND only when the target is one of our own units. MISSION_MOVE_TO_UNIT's iData1/iData2 pair is a player ID and a unit ID, NOT a coordinate (CvSelectionGroup.cpp:1473) - which is why it gets its own field rather than being folded into `destination`, where it would export as a plausible but entirely wrong map position. When the target belongs to another player the field is omitted and only `type` is exported: foreignUnits[] deliberately carries no id at all, so there would be nothing to join against, and a stable rival unit ID is exactly the cross-turn memory the engine does not keep and this export does not invent.

cities.description: The player's own cities, with internals only the owner can see. Per-turn rates are game-computed - the harness never re-derives them from rules data.

id.description: Engine city ID, stable across turns.

foodPerTurn.description: Net food surplus (CyCity.foodDifference); negative = starving, 0 while the city is in disorder.

producing.description: Current build; null when nothing queued.

productionNeeded.description: Total hammer cost of current build; null when producing is null and also when producing is a PROCESS_ (a process converts hammers indefinitely and never completes - the engine reports MAX_INT for both cases).

productionPerTurn.description: Hammers per turn as the city screen shows them (CyCity.getCurrentProductionDifference(bIgnoreFood=False, bOverflow=True), i.e. with food-to-hammer conversion and overflow included). Always equals productionFromHammers + productionFromFood, which decompose it; see those. On the turn right after a build completes this includes one-off carried-over overflow, so it is not a steady-state rate.

productionFromHammers.description: The hammer half of productionPerTurn: what the city produces from worked-tile production regardless of what is queued, i.e. getCurrentProductionDifference(bIgnoreFood=True, bOverflow=True). This is the rate an ORDINARY build receives. Exported rather than left to the harness because it is not recoverable from a single turn's file by any other route: while a food build is queued, productionPerTurn already contains the food and foodPerTurn reads 0, so nothing in the file separates the two halves - and last turn's figure does not decompose this one, because worked tiles change (in the baseline run Lisbon's hammers move 8 to 2 across t37-t38). Carries the same one-off overflow caveat as productionPerTurn, and reads 0 during disorder.

productionFromFood.description: The food half of productionPerTurn: food surplus converted into hammers, 0 unless the city is currently training a unit built from food. Non-zero means the city has stopped growing and the build is landing sooner - the trade a reader needs to see. Obtained the way the game's own production bar obtains it (CvCity::getProductionBarPercentages computes exactly getCurrentProductionDifference(False, True) - getCurrentProductionDifference(True, True) to size its two-tone bar), so this is the engine's own decomposition rather than one the mod invents; bFoodProduction gates exactly one additive term inside getProductionDifference and changes nothing else, so the two calls subtract cleanly in every state. NOT derivable from CIV4UnitInfos.xml alone: the engine's test (CvCity::isFoodProduction) is the unit's bFood flag OR a civic with isMilitaryFoodProduction (Police State) making every military unit food-fed, so the qualifying set is wider than the XML flag. Only an ORDER_TRAIN can qualify at all - buildings, projects and processes never consume food. 0 during disorder, when both halves are 0.

cultureThreshold.description: Culture needed for next border expansion.

workedTiles.description: [x, y] of every tile this city has a citizen working, including the city centre (which is worked for free and does produce yield). Sorted. Lives here rather than on map tiles because we only ever iterate our own cities, so no rival's worked tiles can leak - CyPlot.isBeingWorked() is live truth with no visibility check, and the engine's fog-aware wrapper is not exposed to Python. The tiles a city COULD work are not listed: that is the 5x5 square around it minus the four corners (NUM_CITY_PLOTS is 21), so the harness can derive it. Specialists are the citizens left over: population + 1 - len(workedTiles).

buildings.description: Buildings already standing in this city, sorted. The prerequisite half of 'what can this city build now': a building is gated on its tech and on its prerequisite BUILDING, and only this section answers the second - it also prevents recommending something the city already has. BUILDING_ keys, deliberately NOT the BUILDINGCLASS_ keys the wonders section uses: there the limit is a property of the class, so the class is the right key, whereas here what matters is the actual thing standing in the city with its real effects (Portugal's Feitoria and a generic Trading Post share a class but are not the same building). The two are NOT interconvertible by string surgery - 28 stock buildings have a class whose name differs from their own, several many-to-one (BUILDING_COAL_PLANT, BUILDING_HYDRO_PLANT and BUILDING_NUCLEAR_PLANT are all BUILDINGCLASS_FACTORY) - so if a class key is ever needed it must be exported as its own field rather than derived from this one. Expect BUILDING_PALACE in the capital from turn 0. No fog concern: our own cities. Rivals' buildings are absent from foreignCities by design, which exports only what the nameplate shows.

bonuses.description: Resources connected TO THIS CITY, in the same three groups as player.bonuses (see there for how each group is derived). Membership only - no counts, because quantity is an empire-level fact and a city either has the connection or does not. Read via CyCity.hasBonus, the engine's own 'is this resource connected here' test, which already folds in everything: revealed by the right tech, improved with the right improvement, linked by road/river/coast to this city, not severed by war and not traded away. That makes it the right question for 'can this city build an Axeman' and deliberately NOT a diagnosis - it cannot say WHY something is missing. Distinguishing 'no copper anywhere' from 'copper in the fat cross but unroaded' means joining map.tiles (bonus, improvement, route) against this. No fog concern: our own cities, our own trade network.

coastal.description: Whether this city is on the coast, i.e. whether a Harbour, Lighthouse or any naval unit is possible here at all - a hard gate on a whole branch of what the city can build. CyCity.isCoastal(gc.getMIN_WATER_SIZE_FOR_OCEAN()), the engine's own test, exported rather than left to the harness because the obvious hand-rolled version is subtly wrong: it is not 'is any of the eight neighbours water' but 'is this adjacent to a water body of at least the minimum size', so a city on a two-tile pond is NOT coastal.

wonders.description: Which wonders are gone and which the player has already built. This is the one fact in the file that cannot be derived from anything else exported: whether a world wonder is still available depends on whether some rival completed it, which has nothing to do with our techs, resources or cities. Without it, advice will confidently recommend a wonder that was finished elsewhere ten turns ago. NOT A FOG-OF-WAR LEAK, and this was checked rather than assumed: the game's own Info screen lists every world wonder built anywhere in the world and gates only the BUILDER'S IDENTITY on isHasMet, showing 'Unknown' for the civ and city of an unmet builder while showing the wonder itself unconditionally - and every player gets a global popup the moment any world wonder completes. So 'this wonder is taken' is public knowledge while 'Hammurabi built it in Babylon' is not, and this section exports the former only: no owner, no city, no date. Both lists hold BUILDINGCLASS_ keys rather than BUILDING_ ones, because the limit is a property of the class and the class is what a civ's unique replacement shares (a Ziggurat and a Courthouse are one class).

built.description: World wonders (building classes with iMaxGlobalInstances 1) completed ANYWHERE in the world, i.e. the ones no longer available to anyone including us. CyGame.getBuildingClassCreatedCount, a game-level counter - deliberately not a sweep of rivals' cities, which would need their city lists and would in any case miss wonders in cities the player has never seen.

national.description: National wonders (building classes with iMaxPlayerInstances 1) THIS PLAYER has built, from CyPlayer.getBuildingClassCount. Rivals' national wonders are absent because they are neither public nor relevant - one civ building the Heroic Epic uses nothing up for anyone else. Expect BUILDINGCLASS_PALACE here from turn 0: the Palace really does carry iMaxPlayerInstances 1 and every player starts with one, so it is a correct entry rather than a glitch - the list is 'one-per-civ classes we own', which the Palace is.

map.description: Every tile the player's team has ever revealed, in row-major (y, then x) order - array order only, unaffected by which direction y increases (see the top-level description's COORDINATES note: y increases SOUTH here, opposite the game engine's own y-up). Full snapshot each turn, no diffs. Tiles without visibleNow are revealed but fogged - remembered, possibly stale info, exactly what the player's own map shows. FIELD OMISSION IS MEANINGFUL HERE: only x, y, terrain and yields are always written; every other field is omitted when it equals the `default` recorded below. This is a different sense of omission from a missing top-level SECTION, which means the mod does not build it yet. STALENESS: on a fogged tile, improvement, route and owner are what the player last saw and may be out of date, because those three are the only things the engine remembers per team. Terrain, feature, bonus, river and the rest have no remembered variant and are always current - which is also what the game's own tile mouseover shows, so this matches the UI rather than being more or less informed than it.

plotType.description: Peak / hills / water / flat land are ONE engine enum (CvPlot::m_ePlotType), not independent flags, so this is one field and the four values are mutually exclusive by construction. Omitted for PLOT_LAND, plain flat land. Names are the game's own, from the PlotTypes enum in CvEnums.h - but this is the schema's single exception to 'every enum-like value is an XML Type key': plot type has no XML info object, so there is nothing to join against and the harness must know these four names. PLOT_PEAK is an impassable mountain; PLOT_OCEAN is any water tile, coast or ocean or lake.

lake.description: This water tile is a lake rather than sea. Not derivable from terrain - lakes and coastal sea are both TERRAIN_COAST; it is a property of the plot's area. Lakes give fresh water and health, and cannot be sailed out of.

freshWater.description: Land tile with fresh water: on a river, or adjacent to a lake, or adjacent to a feature that adds fresh water (flood plains, oasis). Enables farms before Civil Service and gives a city founded here extra health. Not derivable from any other field, since the adjacency terms depend on neighbours.

river.description: The tile is on a river - it has a river along at least one of its own edges (CyPlot.isRiver, i.e. getRiverCrossingCount() > 0). Which edge is deliberately not exported: it only affects exact movement cost and the river-attack modifier, both of which belong to the action-execution phase, and the edge data would in any case be incomplete at the boundary of the revealed area.

bonus.description: Resource, read via the team-aware getter: absent both when there is none and when the player lacks the revealing tech. Team-aware but not fog-aware, which is correct - a resource stays visible through fog once revealed.

improvement.description: What the player REMEMBERS being here (getRevealedImprovementType), not what is there now. Goody huts arrive through this field: the engine's own isRevealedGoody() is just improvementInfo(revealed improvement).isGoody().

route.description: Road or railroad the player remembers (getRevealedRouteType).

owner.description: Owning player ID as the player remembers it (getRevealedOwner); absent when unowned or never seen owned. This is what draws the player's borders.

visibleNow.description: Present and true only while the tile is actually in sight of a unit or city. Absent means revealed but fogged, so the remembered fields above may be stale. Most revealed tiles are fogged, so the rare case is the one written.

yields.description: [food, production, commerce] exactly as the game displays them - calculateYield(bDisplay=True), which is what both the map's yield icons and the tile mouseover pass, and which uses the revealed improvement/route/owner internally. Two inherited surprises: a plot with no land anywhere in its 21-tile city cross reports [0, 0, 0] whatever it is (deep ocean therefore looks barren, which is what the map shows); and on an unowned tile the engine substitutes the active player as owner, so trait effects like Financial's extra commerce are applied to land nobody owns (again, what the map shows).

contacts.description: Rival civs the player has met, in player-ID order. BARBARIANS AND MINOR CIVS ARE DELIBERATELY EXCLUDED AND THIS IS NOT COSMETIC: their teams declare war on every civ team during CvGame::initDiplomacy, and CvTeam::declareWar calls meet(), so isHasMet and isAtWar are both TRUE for the barbarians from turn 0 - a loop written on isHasMet alone reports a barbarian 'contact', at war, in every export from turn 1. The filter is the base game's own: isAlive() and not isBarbarian() and not isMinorCiv() and isHasMet(). Met civs since destroyed also drop out, matching those screens. Nothing here is gated on more than having met; no espionage is involved in showing a met civ's attitude.

attitude.description: Their attitude toward the player - the five-bucket value the UI shows (FURIOUS/ANNOYED/CAUTIOUS/PLEASED/FRIENDLY), read as CyPlayer.AI_getAttitude and resolved through gc.getAttitudeInfo, so it joins CIV4AttitudeInfos.xml like every other enum here. The underlying numeric score is NOT exported and could not be: AI_getAttitudeVal is not part of the Python API at all, so the bucket is the most the mod could leak even by accident.

foreignUnits.description: Every other player's units standing on a CURRENTLY-VISIBLE tile, sorted by owner then position. Unlike cities, units are not remembered: the game forgets an enemy stack the moment the tile fogs over, and so does this section - a unit vanishing between turns means 'no longer in sight', not 'destroyed'. The rule is the base game's own, from the military advisor: plot.isVisible(team, False) and not unit.isInvisible(team, False). Invisibility is close to a no-op in the first twenty turns - only the Spy and Great Spy are permanently invisible - but is honoured because it also hides units loaded as cargo, which the map does not draw either. BARBARIANS BELONG HERE and are the main military fact of the early game; they appear under the engine's barbarian player ID, the last player index (MAX_CIV_PLAYERS). FIELD OMISSION IS MEANINGFUL HERE: damage is written only when the unit is hurt.

owner.description: Owning player ID as the game DISPLAYS it (CyUnit.getVisualOwner), not the true owner. The two differ only for hidden-nationality units, which the game shows as barbarian unless they are in one of their owner's cities - no such unit exists before Astronomy, but reading the visual owner means the export can never be the thing that unmasks one.

damage.description: Percentage of health lost, same scale as units[].damage; omitted when the unit is undamaged. Legitimately visible: the engine folds every unit's damage into the stack strength it prints in the tile mouseover, gated only on the plot being visible and with no owner check.

foreignCities.description: Every other player's cities that the player's team has actually laid eyes on, sorted by owner then position. Unlike units, cities persist once seen - the nameplate stays on the map under fog, and so do they here. The gate is CyCity.isRevealed(team, False), a per-city flag STRICTER than the tile being revealed: a city founded on a tile the player revealed long ago but cannot currently see is not revealed to them until they next look. That is why this iterates each rival's own city list rather than sweeping plots and calling getPlotCity(), which reads live truth and would surface those fog-founded cities. Barbarian cities appear on the same terms. The fields are LIVE rather than remembered, which matches the UI rather than overstating it: the engine builds the nameplate from getName(), getPopulation() and isStarCity() with no visibility gate, while deliberately gating the food and production bars beside them on canBeSelected(). Nothing about a city's insides is exported, because nothing about it is shown.

capital.description: This is the owner's capital, which the game marks with a star on the city nameplate (CvCity::isStarCity is literally 'return isCapital()', exported for the renderer and ungated by team or visibility). Omitted when false. Whether the player is currently looking is derivable rather than duplicated here: a revealed city always sits on a revealed tile, so join x/y against map.tiles and read visibleNow.
